DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
# Review: Vendor Comparison, Standard Parcel Delivery Contract (Larkspur Home)

**What the author claims:**
- A fair two-month randomised trial.
- ParcelLine is cheapest, saving £35,000–£76,000 a year.
- All three carriers cleared the 95% on-time threshold.
- ParcelLine's tracking app halved "where is my order?" (WISMO) contacts.
- The 12-month term gives flexibility.

**Bottom line:** the trial design is good and the price arithmetic is correct. But the recommendation is contradicted by the paper's own Table 1:
- **ParcelLine failed two of the four requirements.** On-time delivery was **93.1%**, against a 95% minimum. The damage rate was **0.9%**, against a 0.5% maximum.
- **Once the paper's own £48 cost per damaged or lost parcel is included, ParcelLine becomes the most expensive option**, by about **£6,500–£7,500 a month**.
- **The fall in WISMO contacts can't be credited to the tracking app.** ParcelLine parcels alone carried the new proactive text message from 1 May, so half its trial period had an advantage the others didn't.

On the paper's own figures, **SwiftDrop** is the best fit: it meets every requirement and has the lowest total cost.

## What checks out

| Check | Calculation | Document |
|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop cost per parcel | 0.7 × £3.10 + 0.3 × £4.60 | £3.55 ✓ |
| ParcelLine cost per parcel | 0.7 × £2.85 + 0.3 × £4.95 | £3.48 ✓ |
| Meridian cost per parcel | 0.7 × £3.30 + 0.3 × £4.40 | £3.63 ✓ |
| Monthly delivery costs | 42,000 × the figures above | £149,100 / £146,160 / £152,460 ✓ |
| Annual savings | £2,940 × 12; £6,300 × 12 | £35,280 / £75,600 ✓ |
| WISMO saving against SwiftDrop | (11 − 6) per 1,000 × 42,000 × £3.20 | ~£670 ✓ |

---

## 1. ParcelLine did not meet the service requirements

Section 3 says on-time delivery was "above 95% for all three carriers during the trial". Table 1 shows otherwise:

| Requirement | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-time ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✓ | **93.1% ✗** | 97.5% ✓ |
| Damage < 0.5% | 0.4% ✓ | **0.9% ✗** | 0.3% ✓ |
| Full tracking | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Returns service | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

**These failures aren't trial noise.** With about 5,000 parcels per carrier, the 95% confidence intervals are roughly:
- ParcelLine on-time: **92.4–93.8%**, well below 95%;
- ParcelLine damage: **0.64–1.16%**, well above 0.5%.

The damage rate isn't mentioned anywhere in the paper's discussion or recommendation, even though Section 2 calls damage commercially important and the most common cause of one-star reviews.

## 2. Including damage and loss reverses the cost ranking

Section 2 puts the cost of each damaged or lost parcel at £48. Applying that to the trial rates:

| Monthly cost | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery charges | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damage and loss (rate × 42,000 × £48) | £8,670 (0.43%) | £19,760 (0.98%) | £6,450 (0.32%) |
| WISMO contacts (× £3.20) | £1,480 | £810 | £1,340 |
| **Total** | **£159,250** | **£166,720** | **£160,250** |

- **ParcelLine costs about £7,500 a month more than SwiftDrop**, roughly **£90,000 a year**. It costs about £6,500 a month more than Meridian.
- That is before any cost from one-star reviews, and before counting late deliveries, which aren't costed here.
- The table counts ParcelLine's WISMO advantage in full. Even so, it doesn't come close to closing the gap.

The lost-parcel rates rest on small numbers: at 5,000 parcels each, about 4 lost for ParcelLine against 1–2 for the others. But damage drives nearly all of the difference, and the damage figures are robust.

## 3. The WISMO reduction can't be credited to the app

Section 5 says "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts". The same section then says that from 1 May, **only ParcelLine parcels** carried the new proactive delivery-day text. That is half the trial, and the change most likely to reduce "where is my order?" contacts.

- The effect of the app and the effect of the text can't be separated as reported.
- It is also notable that ParcelLine, with **more late deliveries**, generated **fewer** WISMO contacts. Late deliveries usually cause those contacts, which points to the text message as the main driver.
- **What would settle it:** compare ParcelLine's April contacts (no text) with its May contacts (with text). If the text is rolled out to every carrier, as planned, the difference may largely disappear whichever carrier is chosen.

## 4. Peak season and heavier parcels

- **Season.** The trial ran in April–May. The contract starts on 1 October, so the first months would be peak trading.
  - SwiftDrop and Meridian have peak-season references from retailers of similar size.
  - ParcelLine's references are mainly fashion retailers with lighter parcels.
- **Heavier parcels.** 30% of Larkspur's parcels are 2–10 kg lamps, mirrors and small furniture, which are more likely to be damaged. Breaking the trial's damage rates down by weight band would show whether ParcelLine's problem is concentrated in the heavier items. That seems plausible given its references.

## 5. Contract term

The 12-month term is a fair point in ParcelLine's favour against Meridian. But SwiftDrop offers the same 12 months. Switching carriers also has a cost, so the option to re-tender shouldn't be relied on to fix a weak choice.

---

## What is sound

- **The trial design.** Random allocation by the warehouse system, around 5,000 parcels per carrier, and measurement of on-time, damage and loss is a genuinely fair comparison. The author is right to emphasise it.
- **The price arithmetic.** Every figure in Section 4 is correct.
- **Section 6.** The integration, collection and proof-of-delivery comparisons are useful, and they show no differences between carriers that would change the decision.

## Settled and open

**Settled by the paper's own figures:**
- ParcelLine failed the on-time and damage requirements, and not by a margin that sampling error could explain.
- Including damage and loss at £48 a parcel makes ParcelLine the most expensive option.
- The WISMO difference is confounded with the text-message test.

**Open:**

| Question | What would settle it |
|---|---|
| How much of ParcelLine's WISMO reduction comes from the app? | Its April contacts compared with May |
| Is damage concentrated in the 2–10 kg parcels? | Trial damage rates by weight band |
| SwiftDrop or Meridian? | Whether Meridian's slightly better service (on-time 97.5% against 96.2%) justifies about £1,000 a month more and a 24-month term |

## Recommendation

Revise the paper to:
- correct the on-time statement;
- add damage and loss costs to the comparison;
- remove the claim that the app caused the WISMO reduction.

On the current evidence, **SwiftDrop** should be the recommended carrier. It meets all four requirements, has the lowest total cost, offers a 12-month term, and has peak-season experience. **Meridian** is a reasonable alternative if the Board values its slightly better service enough to accept the 24-month commitment. ParcelLine shouldn't be recommended unless it can show it meets the on-time and damage standards.
